records.title: Mendelian inheritance rediscovery after decades of low uptake
records.sourceNativeSummary: Mendel's 1866 pea results remained low-impact for decades; around 1900 de Vries, Correns and Tschermak independently returned to segregation-style inheritance and Mendel's paper became newly legible inside an active heredity problem. Delayed recognition changed disciplinary interpretation without changing the old experiments.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Later genetics should not project a complete twentieth-century gene theory into Mendel's original text. Low initial uptake does not imply zero evidence value, while eventual rediscovery does not prove every later Mendelian interpretation was already present in 1866.

sources.supports: Mendel experiments/publication and later scientific legacy

records.title: Wegener continental drift proposed at the HD3 boundary before long delayed acceptance
records.sourceNativeSummary: Wegener introduced continental drift as a full scientific theory in 1912 using geographic, fossil and geological correspondences. It faced severe criticism and lacked a convincing mechanism; decades later ocean-floor, paleomagnetic, seafloor-spreading and earthquake evidence transformed the evidentiary world and contributed to plate tectonics.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The later success of plate tectonics does not make Wegener's 1912 mechanism complete or make contemporaneous rejection irrational in every respect. Present non-tractability/missing mechanism can retain future option value, but future vindication must not be back-projected as present proof.

sources.supports: decades of rejection and postwar new evidence

records.antiCase: weak present closure can preserve future explanatory option value

records.title: Railway standard time and International Meridian coordination
records.sourceNativeSummary: Railways and telegraphy made local solar times operationally costly. North American railroads adopted Standard Railway Time in 1883; the 1884 International Meridian Conference then selected a common prime meridian for global longitude/time coordination. A convention became infrastructure because clocks, schedules, observatories, cities and communication networks adopted it.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Greenwich was not physically the uniquely true meridian; it was a coordination choice with installed-use advantages. Standardization can create large system value without turning an arbitrary convention into a natural law.

sources.supports: 1883 railway standard time, four zones and 1884 conference

records.title: International electrical units to IEC cross-industry electrotechnical coordination
records.sourceNativeSummary: Rapidly expanding electrical systems required shared units, terminology, ratings and equipment interfaces across countries and manufacturers. International electrical congresses progressively stabilized units; the International Electrotechnical Commission was founded in 1906 as a continuing international standards organization rather than one product owner.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Standards do not prove one physical architecture globally optimal; they reduce comparison/interconnection cost inside agreed interfaces. Excessive premature standardization can also freeze a local design, so the historical value lies in recurrent interface pressure, not standardization for its own sake.

sources.supports: IEC founded in 1906 and international electrotechnical standards role

records.title: Titanic wireless distress traffic and international radiotelegraph safety rules
records.sourceNativeSummary: Titanic's 1912 sinking exposed that radio range alone was insufficient for maritime safety: operators, distress priority, watch periods, common wavelength and willingness/interoperability to relay messages mattered. The London conference later that year strengthened operating rules around distress communications.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The disaster does not show wireless technology failed as a communication capability; it shows a capable medium can still fail at system-level coordination. Technical availability, operator attention and international operating obligations are separate axes.

sources.supports: 1912 London conference, distress priority, common wavelength and listen intervals
Titanic response and ship-radio watch rules

records.title: Triangle Shirtwaist fire and factory/fire-safety reform pressure
records.sourceNativeSummary: The 1911 Triangle fire killed 146 workers within minutes amid locked/poorly usable exits and inadequate fire escape/ladders. Public inquiry created the New York Factory Investigating Commission; 1912–13 legislation expanded fire-safety, building and labor enforcement requirements.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Rules existed before the fire against locked doors, yet effective safety was absent. Written prohibition, employer compliance, inspection/enforcement and physical egress are distinct. Later law also did not make all future factory fires disappear.

sources.supports: Factory Investigating Commission and systemic factory hazards

records.title: Carbon microphone/transmitter as a hidden telephone-network complement
records.sourceNativeSummary: Early Bell-type telephones could transmit speech, but carbon-resistance transmitters greatly increased practical loudness and line performance. Edison demonstrated carbon transmitters publicly in 1878 and patent models preserve the component architecture; this seemingly small component materially expanded the viable network envelope.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A better transmitter did not invent switching, line engineering or network business. Conversely, a famous network can hide component bottlenecks whose improvement changes system reach without changing the headline product identity.

sources.supports: 1878 National Academy demonstration of carbon transmitters
